title: Bitcoin ordinals and inscriptions drive on-chain activity su
content:
TL;DR: The Bitcoin network is buzzing with activity, driven by the persistent demand for Ordinals and Inscriptions, pushing transaction fees higher and emphasizing Bitcoin's utility beyond mere value storage. This surge in on-chain engagement, even with a recent dip in hashrate to 848.62 EH/s and a difficulty of 146.47 T, underscores the protocol's adaptability and reinforces its role as the hardest, most resilient money. Transactors should monitor mempool dynamics closely and consider fee-bumping strategies for time-sensitive movements, while miners benefit from a robust fee market that complements block subsidies.

The Report

As of February 01, 2026, at 23:56 UTC, the Bitcoin network continues its relentless operation, reaching block height 934,660. The current hashrate stands at a robust 848.62 EH/s, demonstrating the ongoing commitment of global mining operations to secure the network. While this figure represents a slight decrease from the approximately 977 EH/s observed just last week on January 23rd, it still signifies an immense computational effort dedicated to validating transactions and enforcing the protocol's rules. The network's difficulty, currently at 146.47 T, remains a formidable barrier to any would-be attacker, though it is important to note this is below the November 2025 peak of 155.9 T. The next difficulty adjustment is 62.1% complete, with 764 blocks remaining until the next recalibration, which will likely see a downward adjustment given the recent hashrate dip, ensuring block times remain consistent.

The primary driver of current on-chain activity and the prevailing fee market conditions continues to be the sustained interest in Bitcoin Ordinals and Inscriptions. These digital artifacts, etched directly onto individual satoshis, have transformed Bitcoin into a canvas for digital collectibles, identity, and even rudimentary applications. This phenomenon has led to a significant increase in transaction volume and, consequently, a more competitive fee environment. Data from mempool.space frequently shows persistent demand, with average transaction fees often elevated compared to historical norms before the advent of Ordinals. This surge is not merely speculative; it represents a fundamental shift in how some users perceive and utilize Bitcoin's block space, moving beyond simple monetary transfers to include the creation and transfer of unique digital assets.

Globally, the narrative around digital assets is increasingly bifurcated. While traditional financial institutions grapple with the implications of central bank digital currencies (CBDCs) and the ongoing geopolitical shifts, Bitcoin quietly demonstrates its utility as an uncensorable, permissionless ledger. The Ordinals movement, controversial to some purists, inadvertently highlights Bitcoin's adaptability and its capacity to absorb new use cases without altering its core monetary policy. This organic evolution contrasts sharply with the top-down, politically motivated changes seen in traditional finance.
